mission: Make real-world scams visible — including modern AI-enabled fraud — so people can defend themselves and warn others.

threats.title: Apple / iCloud Support & Device-Lock Scams
threats.summary: Pop-ups, texts, or calls claim your iCloud is locked or your iPhone was found. Goal: Apple ID password, 2FA codes, or remote screen-sharing that drains accounts.
how_it_works: Browser pop-up: 'Your iPhone has been compromised — call this number.'
SMS with link to fake iCloud unlock page.
Caller pretends to be Apple; asks for 6-digit code (that's your real 2FA).
real_world: Elder fraud hotlines report Apple support as a top vishing script.
Lost-device phishing: 'We found your phone, verify ownership here.'
red_flags: Apple never asks for 2FA codes by phone or SMS.
Pressure to install AnyDesk / TeamViewer 'for support'.
Threat to permanently lock device today.
what_to_do: Hang up; contact Apple via official app or apple.com only.
Settings → Apple ID → Sign-In & Security → review devices.
If code was given: change Apple ID password immediately, sign out other sessions.
threats.tell_others: Apple will never call asking for a six-digit code on your phone. That code unlocks your account for the scammer.

threats.title: Credential Stuffing & Password Reuse
threats.summary: Passwords leaked in one breach are automatically tried on banks, email, and social accounts. No phishing needed if you reused passwords.
how_it_works: Billions of credential pairs sold from old breaches.
Bots test Netflix, Gmail, Coinbase, corporate VPN.
Successful hits sold or used for further fraud.
Combo with MFA fatigue if password alone insufficient.
real_world: Have I Been Pwned tracks billions of accounts.
Most 'hacked' consumer accounts are stuffing, not genius hackers.
Enables SIM swap follow-up when email compromised.
red_flags: Login alert from city you've never visited.
Password reset emails you didn't trigger.
Friends report spam from your account.
what_to_do: Unique password per site via password manager.
Enable MFA on email first — it's the recovery hub.
Check haveibeenpwned.com; rotate exposed passwords.
threats.tell_others: If you use the same password everywhere, one leak unlocks all accounts. Use a password manager — it's the single best fix.

threats.title: Google / Microsoft 'Sign In' & OAuth Consent Scams
threats.summary: Fake login pages steal passwords, or trick you into approving a malicious OAuth app that reads email, contacts, and files without needing your password again.
how_it_works: Link looks like accounts.google.com or login.microsoftonline.com but one character is wrong.
After password entry, a real-looking 'Allow app' screen grants attacker API access.
Stolen session cookies skip MFA on some flows if device is already 'trusted'.
real_world: Business email compromise often starts with a convincing Microsoft 365 login.
Crypto and bank recovery scams use Google 'security alert' templates.
Free cloud storage / document share lures ('View invoice').
red_flags: Login URL bar doesn't match exactly: google.com vs google-verify.com.
App permission request from unknown publisher.
Urgent 'account will close in 24h' language.
what_to_do: Check signed-in devices at myaccount.google.com / account.microsoft.com.
Revoke unknown third-party app access.
Enable hardware security key or passkey on primary accounts.
Use password manager — it won't autofill on lookalike domains.
threats.tell_others: Never log in from an email link. Open a new tab and type google.com or apple.com yourself. If you already clicked, change password and check 'apps connected to your account'.

threats.title: Instagram / TikTok / Facebook Account Theft
threats.summary: Fake verification, brand deals, or 'copyright strike' DMs trick creators into handing over credentials or 2FA.
how_it_works: 'You're approved for monetization — log in here.'
Fake Meta/TikTok copyright portal.
Attacker changes email/phone, locks victim out, extorts or runs ads.
real_world: Creator economy targeting — stolen accounts sold or used for crypto scams.
Friends receive 'help me vote in this contest' from hijacked account.
red_flags: Login page opened from in-app browser DM link.
Request to screenshot your 2FA code for 'verification'.
what_to_do: Only change account settings inside official app → Settings.
Enable login alerts; review trusted devices.
Backup codes stored offline before incident.
threats.tell_others: No brand deal needs your password in a DM link. Meta and TikTok verify inside the app, not random websites.

threats.title: MFA Push Bombing & Fatigue
threats.summary: After password leak, attacker triggers dozens of MFA push notifications hoping you tap Approve to make it stop.
how_it_works: Credential from breach used on corporate SSO.
Repeated push / call MFA prompts.
User approves accidentally or out of annoyance.
real_world: Documented in Microsoft 365 and Okta intrusion chains.
Often paired with help-desk vishing ('approve the prompt we just sent').
red_flags: MFA prompts when you aren't logging in.
IT call immediately after unexplained push.
what_to_do: Deny unknown prompts; report to IT.
Use number matching / geofenced MFA policies.
Change password if pushes persist.
threats.tell_others: If your phone buzzes with login approvals you didn't start, tap Deny and tell IT. Never approve to silence notifications.

threats.title: SIM Swap & Phone Number Takeover
threats.summary: Attacker convinces your mobile carrier to port your number to their SIM, then receives SMS 2FA codes and password resets for bank, email, and crypto.
how_it_works: Social engineer carrier store or online account recovery.
Once number ports, attacker triggers 'forgot password' on your accounts.
SMS-based 2FA becomes the weak link.
real_world: High-profile crypto and bank losses tied to SIM swaps.
Data broker info (DOB, last 4 SSN) used to answer carrier security questions.
red_flags: Sudden loss of cell service while phone shows 'no signal' in a good area.
Carrier texts about number transfer you didn't request.
what_to_do: Carrier PIN / port lock / account lock feature (AT&T Port Lock, Verizon Number Lock, etc.).
Move 2FA to authenticator app or hardware key — not SMS.
If swapped: call carrier fraud line immediately, then banks.
threats.tell_others: Text-message codes for banking are weak. Use an authenticator app. Put a port-lock PIN on your phone account at the carrier.

threats.title: Session Hijacking & Adversary-in-the-Middle (Even With MFA)
threats.summary: Reverse-proxy phishing captures session cookies after real MFA login — attacker inherits your session without stealing password. Passkeys help but aren't universal yet.
how_it_works: Fake login proxies to real Microsoft/Google; relays MFA prompt.
Victim completes real MFA; attacker gets session token.
Mailbox rules added silently for BEC persistence.
Variant: malware steals browser cookie stores.
real_world: Evilginx-class kits widely documented in defender training.
Corporate M365 intrusions often start here.
Consumers hit via fake parcel or shared-doc links.
red_flags: Login URL not exact official domain even if padlock shows.
Unexpected MFA right after unrelated email click.
New devices in account security panel you don't recognize.
what_to_do: Use passkeys/hardware keys where supported — bind to real domain.
Review active sessions and revoke unknown devices.
Enterprise: phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2), conditional access.
threats.tell_others: Even if you typed your password and MFA correctly, a fake login page can still steal your session. Check the URL letter-by-letter.

threats.title: AI Deepfake Sextortion & Nude Blackmail
threats.summary: Attackers generate fake intimate images from innocent photos (social media, video calls) or claim to have webcam footage, then demand payment to avoid sharing with contacts.
how_it_works: Face-swap or diffusion models create fake nudes from Instagram/LinkedIn headshots.
Email includes real password from old breach as 'proof' they hacked you.
Variant: trick into video chat, record, or deploy malware — less common than pure bluff/fake.
Payment in crypto or gift cards; threats escalate on timer.
real_world: FBI and NCMEC public warnings on AI-generated sextortion targeting teens and adults.
Teen suicide cases linked to sextortion pressure campaigns.
Mass spam: same template sent to millions with generic fake images.
red_flags: Sender won't prove possession with specific uncropped original only you would have.
Demands payment urgently; threatens to email employer/family list.
Image artifacts: wrong skin tone at hairline, extra fingers, blurry face swap.
what_to_do: Do not pay — payment marks you for repeat targeting.
Save evidence; report to FBI IC3, local police, platform abuse.
Teens: tell a trusted adult immediately — NCMEC CyberTipline.
Tighten social media privacy; limit public high-res face photos.
threats.tell_others: Fake nude blackmail is exploding because of AI. Don't pay. Tell police. Real victims rarely lose control if they don't engage.

threats.title: AI Deepfake Video Calls (Face + Voice on Zoom/Teams)
threats.summary: Real-time or pre-recorded deepfake video impersonates executives on video calls, convincing staff to approve wires or share credentials. Combined with cloned voice, the call feels fully legitimate.
how_it_works: Public CEO/interview footage trains face and voice models.
Live deepfake webcam feed joins a rushed 'emergency' meeting.
Attacker stays silent or uses short loops while accomplice speaks.
Follow-up: 'CFO will send wire details by email' from compromised account.
real_world: 2024 Hong Kong case: deepfake CFO video call led to ~$25M wire (widely reported).
High-value BEC moving from email-only to multimodal impersonation.
Smaller businesses targeted as video tools become commoditized.
red_flags: Video slightly out of sync, odd blinking, or frozen when asked to turn head.
Refusal to use established approval workflow.
New payment account or crypto wallet never used before.
what_to_do: Mandatory callback on known numbers for any wire change.
Secret challenge only real exec would know (not posted online).
Policy: large transfers need in-person or hardware-key approval.
threats.tell_others: A video call isn't proof it's really your boss. Deepfake video scams stole millions in 2024. Call back on a number you already trust.

threats.title: AI Disinformation & Manipulation (Consumer Impact)
threats.summary: AI generates fake news clips, product reviews, and outrage posts to manipulate purchases, elections perceptions, or stock prices — and to lend credibility to scam investments or fake charities.
how_it_works: Bot networks amplify AI-written posts about 'miracle' supplements or coins.
Fake celebrity endorsements using deepfake short videos on social ads.
Coordinated comments push victims toward fraudulent support lines.
Synthetic 'local news' sites cite nonexistent events.
real_world: FTC actions on AI-generated fake reviews (2024 guidance).
Crypto pump schemes use AI news summaries on Telegram.
Health fraud surges around AI-written miracle cure content.
red_flags: Only obscure blogs report 'breaking' financial news.
Celebrity endorsement not on their verified account.
Comments disabled or all uniformly positive on investment posts.
what_to_do: Cross-check financial claims with SEC, FCA, or national regulators.
Use official celebrity/brand channels only.
Teach family to verify before sharing outrage content.
threats.tell_others: AI can fake news clips and reviews. Before you invest or donate based on a viral post, check an official source.

threats.title: AI-Assisted Romance & Pig-Butchering Scams
threats.summary: Long-con 'relationship' built on WhatsApp/Telegram leads to fake investment platforms. AI chatbots maintain 24/7 conversation, translate, and script emotional manipulation while human operators handle money.
how_it_works: Wrong-number or dating-app opener → weeks of daily messages.
AI keeps victim engaged overnight; human takes over for money asks.
Shows fake trading app with fabricated gains; victim deposits crypto.
Platform blocks withdrawals; 'taxes' or 'fees' demanded repeatedly.
real_world: FBI IC3: crypto investment fraud among top loss categories (billions annually).
Scam compounds ('pig butchering') often run from forced-labor compounds — victims on both sides.
AI lowers operator cost per target, increasing volume.
red_flags: Never met in person; always excuses; pushes exclusive investment tip.
App not in official App Store listing or sideload required.
Profits show before you understand the product; small withdrawals allowed then blocked.
what_to_do: Never invest via link from someone you only know online.
Verify apps only through official store + known regulator registration.
If money sent: report IC3.gov, bank, and crypto exchange immediately — recovery scams follow.
threats.tell_others: If an online friend teaches 'secret' crypto investing on a special app, it's almost always a scam — AI helps them text you all day now.

threats.title: AI-Drafted Malware Lures (Docs, Invoices, Job PDFs)
threats.summary: Professional-looking invoices, HR policies, and résumés — grammatically perfect — deliver macros, ISO/IMG mounts, or links to password-protected malware. AI removes traditional 'bad formatting' tells.
how_it_works: Password-protected ZIP bypasses scanners; password in email body.
HTML smuggling or OneNote/ISO attachments on Windows.
Fake job offer PDF with 'application form' link to stealer.
LLM localizes lure to regional tax or legal terminology.
real_world: Threat intel: QBot/Emotet campaigns adopted polished lures post-LLM era.
Job seekers targeted with tailored role descriptions from scraped postings.
Small businesses receive fake vendor invoice chains.
red_flags: Unexpected attachment from unknown sender.
Enable macros / disable protected view prompts.
Invoice numbers you can't match to PO.
what_to_do: Open attachments only after verifying sender out-of-band.
Disable macros by default; use PDF viewer without auto-execute.
Sandbox or cloud-scan unknown files before opening locally.
threats.tell_others: Perfect-looking invoice PDFs can still carry viruses. Call the vendor on a known number before opening attachments.

threats.title: AI-Generated Phishing (Perfect Grammar, Personalised Lures)
threats.summary: Large language models write convincing phishing emails and texts in any language, with no spelling mistakes, tailored to your LinkedIn role, local events, or breached data. Filters trained on 'bad grammar' miss them.
how_it_works: Attacker feeds your name, employer, and breach data into an LLM to draft a bespoke lure.
AI clones tone of real vendors (DocuSign, FedEx, payroll) and references plausible internal projects.
Translated campaigns hit non-English speakers at native fluency.
Same kit mass-produces thousands of variants to evade signature-based detection.
real_world: Security vendors documented LLM-written BEC and HR/payroll lures from 2023 onward.
Hybrid campaigns: AI draft + human polish for high-value targets.
SMS and LinkedIn DM variants use the same generated scripts.
red_flags: Email feels 'too perfect' yet still pushes urgency or credential entry.
References real colleagues or projects scraped from public profiles.
Link domain still wrong on close inspection — AI doesn't fix malicious URLs.
what_to_do: Judge actions, not writing quality: never auth via email links.
Report suspicious mail with headers; don't reply.
Organizations: train on behavioral cues (unexpected requests), not typos alone.
threats.tell_others: Scammers use ChatGPT-style tools now — perfect spelling doesn't mean an email is real. Still never log in from a link.

threats.title: Malicious AI Chatbots Pretending to Be Bank or Tech Support
threats.summary: Fake support sites embed AI chat that mimics Apple, Amazon, or your bank — guiding you to install remote access tools, reveal OTP codes, or visit credential-harvesting pages.
how_it_works: Ads or poisoned search results for 'Amazon customer service number'.
Chatbot asks for order details then 'verifies' with login link.
Escalates to human scammer or scripted remote-access flow.
Logs entire conversation for reuse in spear phishing.
real_world: Google Ads abuse for fake support remains top consumer fraud vector.
AI chat lowers staffing cost for scam call centers.
Mobile users hit via in-app browser overlays.
red_flags: Support initiated from ad or pop-up, not official app.
Chat asks for password, OTP, or remote access.
URL is support-helpdesk-secure.com style domain.
what_to_do: Contact companies only via official app or typed domain.
Never install remote tools for unsolicited support.
Bookmark real support URLs in password manager notes.
threats.tell_others: Google the support number and you may get a fake AI chatbot. Use the phone number on your card or inside the official app only.

threats.title: Real-Time AI Voice Cloning on Live Phone Calls
threats.summary: Beyond pre-recorded clips, low-latency AI can hold a short conversation sounding like a relative, bank officer, or IT help desk — answering simple prompts while pushing you to approve MFA or transfer money.
how_it_works: 3–10 seconds of voice from TikTok, voicemail, or YouTube trains a clone.
Live call uses speech-to-text → LLM reply → cloned speech output.
Pairs with SIM swap or MFA fatigue: 'I'm IT, approve the prompt I just sent.'
Fails on complex personal questions — attackers avoid deep conversation.
real_world: Multiple documented family-emergency wire cases using cloned child voice (2023–2025).
Banks warn corporate treasury teams after CEO voice fraud attempts.
Consumer robocall 'grandma' variants increasingly AI-driven vs tape loops.
red_flags: Caller insists you must act now and won't pause for callback.
Background noise loop or unnatural pauses before answers.
Ask something only real person knows — clone often deflects.
what_to_do: Family code word for emergencies; never wire without second channel.
Hang up; dial stored contact — not number they give.
Enable call screening; don't trust caller ID.
threats.tell_others: AI can fake a voice live on the phone now. If someone says they're your kid in jail and need wire — hang up and call their real number.

threats.title: Synthetic Identity & AI-Generated Personas
threats.summary: Fraudsters combine real SSN fragments (often minors or deceased) with fake personas — sometimes AI-generated profile photos and résumés — to open credit, launder money, or pass remote job verification.
how_it_works: AI face generators produce unique 'selfies' that pass basic liveness checks.
LLM writes consistent backstory across applications and social profiles.
Used for mule accounts, fraudulent loans, and remote-work hiring fraud.
Deepens pig-butchering trust with fabricated identity across platforms.
real_world: Credit industry reports synthetic identity among fastest-growing fraud types.
Remote hiring scams use AI headshots in video interviews (static image + lip sync).
DPRK IT worker schemes overlap with synthetic persona documentation.
red_flags: New 'employee' or vendor only reachable on encrypted chat apps.
Profile photo too perfect or inconsistent across sites (reverse image empty but AI-detect artifacts).
Payment requests to personal accounts vs business entity.
what_to_do: Employers: verify identity through licensed KYC + video with challenge questions.
Freeze credit for children; monitor SSN alerts.
Don't trust LinkedIn alone for vendor due diligence.
threats.tell_others: Fake people are real now — AI photos and résumés. Businesses hiring remote should verify identity hard, not just LinkedIn.

threats.title: Sextortion (Webcam / Relationship Blackmail)
threats.summary: After intimate content is shared or recorded (dating apps, video chats), extortionists demand money threatening to send images to contacts. Often organized crime; paying rarely ends threats.
how_it_works: Lure via dating platform → move to video chat quickly.
Malware or fake app claims access to contacts/photos.
Countdown timer screenshots sent as pressure.
Some campaigns purely bluff — no real images.
real_world: FBI sextortion task forces; major teen targeting campaigns.
Often cross-border; difficult prosecution but reporting still vital.
Separate from AI deepfake variant — both active.
red_flags: New match pushes video immediately.
Threat email cites old password from breach.
Demands escalate after each payment.
what_to_do: Don't pay; block; report IC3 + platform.
Teens: tell parent/school counselor — not alone.
Document accounts; tighten privacy settings.
threats.tell_others: If someone threatens to share private photos unless you pay — don't pay. Tell police. They count on shame to keep you quiet.

threats.title: Business Email Compromise (BEC) & Invoice Redirect
threats.summary: Compromised or spoofed executive/vendor email instructs finance to wire money, change payroll direct deposit, or pay fake invoices — often after silent mailbox rules hide replies.
how_it_works: Phish employee → create inbox rules forwarding/deleting finance threads.
Spoofed domain: company-secure.com vs company.com.
Vendor email: 'Our bank details changed' with forged PDF.
Payroll diversion: HR receives fake employee bank update.
real_world: FBI IC3: BEC among highest reported business losses yearly.
School districts and municipalities hit by payroll redirect.
AI improves email quality but BEC predates AI — still dominant.
red_flags: Bank detail change via email only.
Urgent confidential wire bypassing normal approvers.
Reply-from address differs on close inspection.
what_to_do: Verify payment changes by phone on known numbers.
Dual control on wires; out-of-band approval.
Disable external auto-forward; monitor mailbox rules.
threats.tell_others: Companies lose millions when someone emails 'pay this invoice to our new account.' Always call the vendor on the number you already have.

threats.title: Online Grooming & Child Exploitation (Defensive Guide)
threats.summary: Predators build trust in games and chats, move to private platforms, solicit images or meetings. AI-generated personas and sextortion amplify teen risk.
how_it_works: Compliments and gifts in Fortnite/Roblox/Discord DMs.
Age regression: predator claims to be teen.
Migration to Snapchat/Telegram 'where parents won't see'.
Escalation to images → sextortion cycle.
real_world: NCMEC CyberTipline millions of reports annually.
FBI Safe Online Surfing education programs.
Gaming platforms increase moderation but gaps remain.
red_flags: Adult or unknown teen wants private chat off-platform.
Requests for photos or secrecy from parents.
Gift cards or account credentials requested.
what_to_do: Parental controls + talk about 'never secret from parents' rules.
Report platform abuse; CyberTipline.org for CSAM.
Preserve evidence; don't delete for police.
threats.tell_others: Teach kids: anyone asking for secret chats or photos online is dangerous — tell an adult immediately. No shame in reporting.

threats.title: DPRK Remote IT Worker & Contractor Impersonation
threats.summary: State-sponsored operatives use stolen or synthetic identities to get hired as remote developers, access employer networks, and funnel salary to sanctioned regimes — or plant access for later intrusion.
how_it_works: Résumé matches real US developer (identity theft or purchase).
Interview lip-sync or proxy speaker; work hours align to obfuscated timezone.
Requests laptop shipment to freight forwarder / mule address.
VPN from laptop into victim employer; GitHub commits from DPRK infrastructure obfuscated.
real_world: FBI/CISA public guidance (2023–2025) on DPRK IT worker schemes.
Tech startups and crypto firms among reported victims.
Overlaps synthetic identity and deepfake interview concerns.
red_flags: Freelancer only on encrypted chat; refuses video with live challenge.
Shipping address ≠ stated residence; VoIP phone only.
Unusual git commit times; shared credentials across 'multiple contractors'.
what_to_do: In-person or live video ID verification for remote hires handling sensitive code.
Ship equipment only to verified addresses; monitor egress.
Report suspicious hiring to FBI local field office.
threats.tell_others: Some 'US developers' hired remotely are fake identities for hostile states. Companies must verify who they're actually hiring.

threats.title: Fake Jobs, Task, & Reshipping Scams
threats.summary: Fake remote jobs pay for 'tasks' (likes, reviews) then require deposits to unlock higher pay — or use you as money mule reshipping stolen goods.
how_it_works: LinkedIn/Indeed offer: easy remote work, high pay.
Initial small payments build trust (your own money cycled back).
Deposit required to 'upgrade' task tier — money gone.
Reshipping mule: receive fraud purchases at your home.
real_world: FTC warnings on task scams targeting students and unemployed.
Package mule networks tied to stolen credit card fraud.
Fake interviews collect ID scans for synthetic identity.
red_flags: Job requires you to pay upfront or buy equipment via their link.
Interview only on Telegram; no company domain email.
Reship packages to unknown third parties.
what_to_do: Verify company registration and careers page on typed domain.
Never pay to work; legitimate employers don't ask.
Report mule activity — legal risk to you.
threats.tell_others: If a job pays you to 'like videos' but first wants a deposit — it's fraud. Real jobs never ask you to pay in.

threats.title: Credit Card & Digital Payment Skimming
threats.summary: Malicious JavaScript on compromised checkout pages steals card numbers. Physical skimmers still exist on ATMs and gas pumps.
how_it_works: E-skimmer injected into real store checkout (Magecart-style).
Fake discount sites capture full PAN + CVV.
Bluetooth overlay on gas pump keypad.
real_world: Major retailer breaches often e-skimmer, not database hack.
Small business WordPress/WooCommerce plugins are frequent entry points.
red_flags: Checkout page looks slightly off-brand.
Prices too good on unknown shop.
ATM slot wiggles or bulky reader.
what_to_do: Use virtual card numbers / wallet tokenization where offered.
Monitor statements; enable transaction alerts.
Pay inside for gas; tug card reader before use.
threats.tell_others: Prefer Apple Pay/Google Pay over typing card numbers on random sites. If a deal needs a unknown shop, it's often a card trap.

threats.title: Crypto Wallet Drainers & Fake Airdrops
threats.summary: Malicious sites ask you to 'connect wallet' and sign a transaction that drains tokens/NFTs, or approve unlimited token spend.
how_it_works: Twitter/X reply bots with fake support links.
Discord DM airdrop claiming free tokens.
Malicious signing request disguised as 'verify wallet'.
real_world: Millions lost via wallet drainer kits sold on underground forums — defenders study patterns to warn users.
Fake Collab.Land and similar Discord verification flows.
red_flags: Site asks for seed phrase (never legitimate).
Unlimited approval for unknown contract.
Time-limited 'claim before midnight'.
what_to_do: Use hardware wallet; review each transaction detail.
Revoke token approvals via reputable chain tools.
Never share seed phrase — ever.
threats.tell_others: No real airdrop needs your seed phrase. Connecting wallet on a link from Discord is how people lose everything.

threats.title: Facebook / Craigslist Marketplace Scams
threats.summary: Fake buyers, fake shipping labels, off-platform payment, and 'verification code' SMS tricks steal money, goods, or account access from local sellers and buyers.
how_it_works: Buyer sends fake PayPal 'paid' email; asks seller to ship.
SMS 'verification code' is actually your account 2FA — they take over.
Fake escrow site linked in chat.
Overpayment Zelle refund trick.
real_world: Platform abuse teams report constant cat-and-mouse.
High-value electronics and vehicles common lures.
Code-forward scam widely documented by carriers.
red_flags: Buyer won't meet locally for high-value item.
Ask to text verification code 'to prove you're real'.
Payment email not from paypal.com domain.
what_to_do: Cash or platform in-person payment for local sales.
Never share SMS codes with strangers.
Ignore 'paid' emails — verify in actual PayPal/bank app.
threats.tell_others: On Marketplace, if someone asks you to text them a code — stop. That code unlocks your account for them.

threats.title: Fake Charities & Disaster Relief Scams
threats.summary: After hurricanes, wars, or viral tragedies, fraudsters spin up fake charities, GoFundMe impersonations, and crypto addresses to capture donations.
how_it_works: Typosquat charity domains and social ads.
Emotional AI-written stories with stolen photos.
Pressure: 'match donation expires tonight'.
Crypto wallet posted as 'official relief fund'.
real_world: State AGs issue warnings after every major disaster.
GoFundMe impersonation via copied campaign links.
Televangelist-style social media fraud overlaps.
red_flags: Charity only accepts crypto, Zelle, or gift cards.
No EIN / registration verifiable on Charity Navigator or regulator.
High-pressure social media DM from unknown org.
what_to_do: Donate via established org typed URL or phone you look up.
Verify GoFundMe organizer identity with mutual contacts.
Credit card donations easier to dispute than crypto.
threats.tell_others: After disasters, fake charities explode. Give only to names you look up yourself — not links in viral posts.

threats.title: Lottery, Sweepstakes & Prize Scams
threats.summary: You're told you won a lottery you never entered — pay fees/taxes upfront to release millions. Or check in mail is fake — overpayment scam when you deposit.
how_it_works: Email/SMS: Publisher's Clearing House or foreign lottery win.
Fee for 'processing', 'customs', or 'lawyer'.
Fake check sent; bank clears provisionally; victim wires 'tax' before bounce.
Jamaican lottery fraud rings (elder targeting, long calls).
real_world: USPS and AARP perennial warnings.
Combines mail fraud + wire + romance elements.
Social media 'giveaway winner' DMs for smaller scams.
red_flags: Win notification for contest you didn't enter.
Pay to receive prize.
Check from unknown entity with instruction to wire portion back.
what_to_do: Real prizes don't require upfront payment.
Wait for check to fully clear (weeks) before acting.
Report to postal inspectors if mail-based.
threats.tell_others: You didn't win a lottery you never entered. Paying 'fees' to get a prize is always a scam.

threats.title: Recovery Scams (Second Victimization)
threats.summary: After initial fraud, new scammers claim they can recover lost crypto or wire funds — for an upfront fee. Victims lose again; some are the same organization.
how_it_works: Cold call: 'We're cyber recovery specialists — saw your report.'
Fake law firm or blockchain tracing company.
Fee for 'tax', 'release', or 'lawyer retainer' before recovery.
Forged documents showing funds 'almost returned'.
real_world: FBI explicitly warns recovery scams follow pig butchering.
Ads target people searching 'recover scammed crypto'.
Some 'recovery' sites are phishing for seed phrases.
red_flags: Guaranteed recovery of crypto sent to scammers.
Upfront fee before any demonstrated legal action.
Asks for seed phrase or remote access to 'trace blockchain'.
what_to_do: Only trust licensed attorneys you initiate contact with.
Report original crime to IC3; ignore recovery spammers.
No legitimate service needs your wallet seed.
threats.tell_others: After a scam, you'll get calls offering to get money back — for a fee. That's the second scam. Talk to police, not cold callers.

threats.title: Rental & Deposit Scams (Fake Listings)
threats.summary: Copied photos of real properties listed cheap; victim pays deposit/wire before viewing; property never existed or wasn't available.
how_it_works: Scrape Zillow/Realtor photos; post on Craigslist/Facebook cheap.
Owner 'abroad' — can't show unit; send deposit to hold.
Fake lease + forged ID; pressure before others 'take it'.
Short-term rental: fake Airbnb links off-platform payment.
real_world: Major city housing crises increase victim volume.
Students and relocating workers primary targets.
AI improves listing description quality.
red_flags: Price far below market.
Can't tour in person or video walkthrough live.
Wire/Zelle/Venmo before signed lease and keys.
what_to_do: Verify owner via county records; tour physically.
Pay through platform escrow only for short stays.
Reverse image search listing photos.
threats.tell_others: If a rental is half price and they want deposit before you walk inside — walk away. See the place and sign real lease first.

threats.title: Subscription Traps & Free-Trial Abuse
threats.summary: Misleading free trials auto-enroll expensive monthly charges; cancellation buried or requires phone call to retention scripts. Not always crime but predatory — some are outright fraud.
how_it_works: Social ad celebrity keto/gummy 'free sample'.
Fine print: $89/month after 14 days.
Card pre-auth for 'shipping' becomes recurring.
Fake antivirus renewal pop-ups.
real_world: FTC cases against recurring billing schemes.
App Store subscription scams in copycat apps.
Elderly less likely to navigate cancellation flows.
red_flags: Card required for 'free' product.
No clear cancel link before purchase.
Charges from unfamiliar merchant descriptor.
what_to_do: Virtual card numbers with spend limits for trials.
Dispute with bank; CFPB/FTC complaints.
Apple/Google subscription settings audit monthly.
threats.tell_others: Free trial that needs your card often becomes $80/month. Read cancel terms first or use a virtual card with a low limit.

threats.title: Travel, Timeshare & Vacation Rental Fraud
threats.summary: Fake airline deals, nonexistent vacation rentals, timeshare resale scams, and TSA PreCheck impersonation steal deposits and personal data.
how_it_works: Too-cheap flights on fake agency site.
VRBO/Airbnb lookalike off-platform wire.
Timeshare: pay fee to sell your share — no sale.
Fake TSA/Global Entry renewal emails.
real_world: BBB scam tracker travel category perennial.
Post-COVID revenge travel surge increased victims.
AI-generated property interiors in fake listings.
red_flags: Wire only; no platform booking protection.
TSA doesn't email payment links for PreCheck.
Resale company guarantees buyer they can't name.
what_to_do: Book airlines/hotels via typed domain or official app.
Stay on platform messaging until check-in verified.
TSA.gov only for PreCheck/Global Entry.
threats.tell_others: If a vacation deal needs wire transfer off Airbnb/VRBO — scam. Book inside the platform or with a card you can charge back.

threats.title: Medicare, Medicaid & Health Insurance Scams
threats.summary: Callers offer 'free' braces, genetic tests, or upgraded plans — harvest Medicare numbers for billing fraud or identity theft. Seniors primary targets.
how_it_works: Cold call: new benefit card or equipment 'at no cost'.
Collect Medicare ID (= SSN on older cards) and ship worthless goods.
Bill Medicare for procedures never done.
Open enrollment confusion exploited with fake plan switches.
real_world: HHS-OIG fraud alerts; billions in improper billing annually.
COVID-era test kit scams evolved into generic health offers.
Door-to-door genetic testing fraud in retirement communities.
red_flags: Unsolicited call offering free medical equipment.
Ask for Medicare number for 'verification'.
Pressure to decide during single call.
what_to_do: Medicare.gov or SHIP counselor for plan questions.
Never give Medicare ID to unsolicited callers.
Review Medicare Summary Notices for unfamiliar charges.
threats.tell_others: Medicare won't call offering free stuff if you give your ID number. That's identity theft and fraud billing.

threats.title: Tax & IRS / HMRC Impersonation
threats.summary: Calls, texts, or letters claim owed taxes, warrants, or refunds — demand immediate payment, gift cards, or bank details. Peak season: filing deadlines.
how_it_works: Robocall + callback to aggressive 'agent'.
Spoofed caller ID: Treasury, IRS, Social Security.
Fake refund portal harvests SSN and bank for 'direct deposit'.
Threat of arrest unless same-day payment.
real_world: IRS publishes annual dirty dozen list — impersonation perennial.
UK HMRC and AU ATO similar campaigns.
AI voice makes calls more convincing.
red_flags: First contact by phone threatening arrest.
Payment via gift card, crypto, or wire.
Email from irs-refund.gov style domains.
what_to_do: IRS initiates by mail; verify at irs.gov only.
Use official tax prep; never click refund status links from email.
Report to Treasury Inspector General (US) or local tax authority.
threats.tell_others: The IRS doesn't call demanding gift cards or threaten immediate arrest. Hang up and go to the official tax website yourself.

threats.title: Data Broker Exposure (Enables Every Other Scam)
threats.summary: Your address, phone, relatives, and purchase history are sold cheaply — scammers use it to make vishing, SIM swap, and spear phishing believable.
how_it_works: People-search sites aggregate public records + breaches.
Scammers buy 'fullz' packages: SSN, DOB, mother's maiden name.
Enables 'Hi [name], I'm calling about your account at [real bank]'.
Geo-targeted quishing and smishing from leaked numbers.
real_world: State delete-my-data laws (CA, etc.) — brokers must comply.
Major breaches (Equifax, telecom) feed underground markets.
OSINT tools make this accessible to non-technical criminals.
red_flags: Caller knows details you never shared — still a scam.
Sudden increase in targeted phishing after breach news.
what_to_do: Opt out of major data brokers (guides online).
Freeze credit at three bureaus + ChexSystems.
Limit public social posts about travel, employer, family.
threats.tell_others: Scammers know your name and address from data brokers — that doesn't mean they're legit. Hang up and call back official numbers.

threats.title: Full Identity Theft (Tax, Medical, Synthetic)
threats.summary: Stolen identity used to open credit, file tax returns, obtain medical care, or commit crimes — victims spend years cleaning records.
how_it_works: Mail theft of pre-approved offers or tax documents.
Phished SSN + ID photos from fake job or gov sites.
Medical ID used for procedures billed to victim.
Child SSN unused for credit — silent for years.
real_world: FTC IdentityTheft.gov primary US recovery portal.
Medical identity theft causes corrupted health records — dangerous in emergencies.
Tax refund fraud peaks before legitimate filers submit.
red_flags: IRS notice of duplicate return.
Medical EOB for doctor you never visited.
Credit denial despite good history.
what_to_do: Credit freeze + fraud alerts.
File FTC report; police report for banks.
IRS Identity Protection PIN if eligible.
threats.tell_others: Shred mail with personal info; freeze kids' credit too. Identity theft is easier to prevent than fix.

threats.title: Pig Butchering (Sha Zhu Pan) — Long-Con Investment Fraud
threats.summary: Victims groomed over weeks/months are steered to fraudulent trading platforms showing fake profits until they deposit life savings — then funds are gone.
how_it_works: Trust phase: daily chat, fake lifestyle photos, shared 'secrets'.
Fattening: small deposits allowed to withdraw once.
Slaughter: large deposit, account frozen, fake taxes demanded.
Operators often victims of trafficking themselves — still report to police.
real_world: Global enforcement actions against scam compounds (SE Asia).
Losses per victim often six figures; retirement funds common.
Overlaps romance, crypto, and forex variants.
red_flags: Platform URL not registered with financial regulator.
Mentor met only on encrypted chat.
Withdrawal requires 'verification deposit' or tax upfront.
what_to_do: Verify broker at regulator site (SEC, FCA, ASIC, etc.).
Stop sending money; document chats and wallet addresses.
Report — do not pay 'recovery hackers' who cold-call afterward.
threats.tell_others: If someone online helped you make money on a trading app and now wants more to unlock withdrawal — it's a scam. Real brokers don't live on WhatsApp.

threats.title: Fake Virus Pop-ups & Remote Access Scams
threats.summary: Browser full-screen pop-up claims virus; phone number connects to scammer who requests remote desktop access and steals files, passwords, and money.
how_it_works: Malvertising or bad extension triggers scary pop-up.
Victim calls; guided to install AnyDesk/TeamViewer.
Attacker browses banking, installs ransomware, or demands gift cards.
real_world: FTC top consumer fraud category for years.
Often targets seniors; payment in gift cards or crypto.
red_flags: Audio alarm from browser tab.
Caller asks for remote access to 'clean virus'.
Payment in iTunes/Google Play gift cards.
what_to_do: Force-quit browser; don't call number on pop-up.
Uninstall unknown remote tools.
Run Guardian / full AV scan locally.
threats.tell_others: Microsoft never puts a phone number on a red virus screen. Close the browser with Task Manager or force quit — don't call.

threats.title: Malicious Browser Extensions & Fake Apps
threats.summary: Extensions and sideloaded apps steal cookies, alter crypto addresses, inject ads, or keylog banking sessions — often disguised as ad blockers, PDF tools, or wallet helpers.
how_it_works: Chrome Web Store extension requests 'read all data on all websites'.
Update channel turned malicious after install base grows.
Android APK outside Play Store mimics wallet or delivery app.
Clipboard hijacker swaps crypto address when you paste.
real_world: Repeated takedowns of popular extension turned malware.
Crypto users lose funds via address swap extensions.
Fake banking apps on third-party stores.
red_flags: Extension from unknown publisher with few reviews.
App requires accessibility + overlay permissions together.
Sideload prompt for 'security update'.
what_to_do: Install only from official stores; review permissions.
Audit extensions quarterly; remove unused.
Verify crypto address first/last chars after paste.
threats.tell_others: Browser add-ons can read everything you type including passwords. Only keep extensions from brands you trust — delete the rest.

threats.title: Ransomware on Personal Devices & Home NAS
threats.summary: Family photos and documents encrypted after malware download, RDP exposure, or compromised NAS. Attackers demand crypto; payment doesn't guarantee decryption.
how_it_works: Email attachment or pirated software delivers payload.
Scans network shares and cloud sync folders.
Deletes shadow copies; exfiltrates data for double extortion.
Consumer routers with default passwords remotely exploited.
real_world: School and hospital headlines — homes hit by same kits.
Qlocker-style NAS ransomware waves.
Some groups publish stolen family data if unpaid.
red_flags: Desktop wallpaper changed to ransom note.
All files renamed .encrypted or similar.
Remote desktop enabled without your knowledge.
what_to_do: Disconnect from network; don't pay immediately.
Restore from offline backup if available.
Report to IC3; check nomoreransom.org for free decryptors.
Prevent: 3-2-1 backups, updates, no exposed RDP.
threats.tell_others: Back up photos to a drive you unplug. Ransomware hits families too — not just companies.

threats.title: Evil Twin Wi‑Fi & Captive Portal Traps
threats.summary: Fake hotspots named 'Free Airport WiFi' or 'Starbucks' intercept traffic or show login pages harvesting email credentials and card numbers for 'premium access'.
how_it_works: Portable router broadcasts trusted SSID name.
Captive portal mimics hotel/airport login.
SSL stripping on poorly configured sites (rarer now).
DNS hijack to phishing banking sites.
real_world: Conference and hotel targeting common in pentest reports.
Travelers lose email → cascade account takeover.
QR-to-WiFi stickers overlap with quishing.
red_flags: Two similarly named networks; neither requires hotel room auth.
Portal asks for email password not just room number.
No WPA2 enterprise when venue normally uses it.
what_to_do: Use phone hotspot or VPN on untrusted Wi‑Fi.
Ask staff for official network name.
Forget network after leaving venue.
threats.tell_others: Free Wi‑Fi with a login that wants your email password is often fake. Use your phone data or ask the hotel for the real network name.

threats.title: Check Fraud, Washing & Mail Theft
threats.summary: Stolen mail checks washed chemically to change payee/amount, or deposited via mobile capture after signature forgery. Business checks high value.
how_it_works: Mailbox fishing or USPS arrow key theft.
Acetone wash removes ink; rewrite amount.
Mobile deposit same check multiple times rapidly.
Fake payroll checks on new accounts (check kiting).
real_world: USPS and banking industry joint warnings 2023–2025 surge.
Small businesses lose rent/check payments from outgoing mail.
Blue USPS collection boxes targeted.
red_flags: Check cleared you didn't write.
Outgoing mail disappeared from box.
Bank alerts on mobile deposit duplicate.
what_to_do: Use gel pen on checks; mail from post office inside.
Switch to ACH/bill pay where possible.
Informed Delivery usps.com to preview incoming mail.
threats.tell_others: Don't leave outgoing checks in home mailbox flag-up. Thieves steal them and rewrite the amount.

threats.title: Gift Card Payment Demands (All Variants)
threats.summary: Any request for payment via gift card numbers is a scam — IRS, bail, tech support, romance, employer, utility shutoff. Cards are resold instantly; untraceable.
how_it_works: Urgent authority figure demands card photos or scratched PINs.
Victim sent store-to-store buying max-value cards.
Scammer drains balance online within minutes.
Variant: 'payroll mistake' employer asks gift card refund.
real_world: FTC: gift cards #1 reported payment method in fraud for years.
Retail staff trained to intervene — still massive losses.
Combines with tech support, government impersonation, sextortion.
red_flags: Any organization requesting gift cards for debt/tax/bail.
Employer or romance partner asks for card numbers.
Stay on phone while purchasing (coached buying).
what_to_do: Stop purchase; hang up.
Tell store clerk if coached — they're trained to help.
Report to FTC and local police if purchased.
threats.tell_others: No real government agency, company, or utility takes gift cards as payment. Ever. If they ask, it's 100% a scam.

threats.title: Zelle / Venmo / Cash App Payment Scams
threats.summary: Scammers exploit irreversible peer-to-peer payments — fake buyer overpays, impersonate bank fraud dept, marketplace 'refund' tricks, or romance requests — knowing chargeback is limited.
how_it_works: Marketplace: fake payment screenshot + 'accidental overpay, refund me'.
Bank impersonation: 'Reverse the Zelle by sending to this safe account'.
Romance/partner 'emergency' needs instant Zelle.
QR at in-person sale redirects payment to wrong recipient.
real_world: CFPB and banks sued over Zelle fraud reimbursement policies.
Elderly targeted via 'fraud department' vishing + Zelle.
Facebook Marketplace scams routinely use P2P.
red_flags: Buyer wants to pay before seeing item with P2P only.
Bank calls asking you to Zelle yourself to 'reverse' fraud.
Refund request to different account than original payer.
what_to_do: P2P only to people you know personally.
Hang up on bank callbacks — call number on card.
If scammed: report immediately; document — recovery unlikely but report anyway.
threats.tell_others: Zelle is like cash — sending to a stranger is gone. Your bank will never ask you to Zelle money to fix fraud.

threats.title: QR Code Phishing (Quishing)
threats.summary: Attackers hide malicious links inside QR codes so email filters and suspicious-URL training miss them. You scan with your phone — outside corporate security — and land on a fake login or malware page.
how_it_works: Email or PDF shows a QR code instead of a clickable link (evades link scanners).
Code opens a credential-harvesting site or app install prompt on mobile.
Some campaigns impersonate payroll, HR, IT, or shipping vendors.
real_world: State-linked campaigns (reported 2023–2025) used quishing in targeted email — often to tech/finance/defense contractors.
Parking-meter and restaurant table QR sticker swaps steal payment card data.
Event flyers and 'free Wi‑Fi' posters with pasted-over QR codes.
red_flags: Unexpected QR in email — legitimate senders rarely require scanning to 'verify' or 'pay'.
QR on a sticker over an original sign in public.
Scan opens a login page for Google, Microsoft, Apple, or your bank.
what_to_do: Type the known website address manually — never scan to reach payroll or banking.
On phones: long-press link preview if available; use company VPN policy for work mail on mobile.
Report phishing to IT; forward headers if your org requests it.
threats.tell_others: If an email says 'scan this QR to fix your account,' stop. Real companies give you a website you can type yourself. QR codes in email are a major 2024–2025 scam pattern.

threats.title: Smishing — Fake Delivery & Toll Texts
threats.summary: Texts claim a package failed, unpaid toll, or customs fee. Link steals card info or installs malware.
how_it_works: Short link + urgency ('final notice').
Mobile-optimized payment page mimics USPS, FedEx, DHL, or state toll authority.
Some variants install Android APK sideload.
real_world: USPS and FBI public alerts on smishing waves 2023–2025.
'You have unpaid tolls' texts tied to credit card skimming pages.
red_flags: Tracking number you don't recognize.
Small payment ($1–3) asked to 'release' parcel — card test then drain.
what_to_do: Track packages only on retailer or carrier site you typed manually.
Delete text; don't reply STOP (confirms active number).
threats.tell_others: Carriers don't text random fee links. Open the store or USPS app directly if you're expecting mail.

threats.title: Contactless NFC / Tap-to-Pay Skimming
threats.summary: Portable readers close enough to tap wallets/pockets, or modified POS terminals, steal contactless card data — usually capped transactions but usable for fraud.
how_it_works: Crowded transit: reader in backpack near cards.
Fake charity tap terminals.
RFID-blocking marketing oversells risk but proximity attacks real in labs.
Relay attacks on car key fobs related technique.
real_world: EU/US banks limit tap amounts; fraud still reported.
Mobile wallet tokenization safer than physical card tap.
ATM shimmer/skimmer hybrids evolve.
red_flags: Unknown charge under contactless limit on statement.
Terminal looks altered or in wrong location.
what_to_do: Use phone wallet with biometric lock.
RFID sleeve if concerned; monitor card notifications.
Report card issuer fraud line immediately.
threats.tell_others: Phone pay with fingerprint is safer than a tap card in your wallet on a crowded train. Turn on instant transaction alerts.

threats.title: USB Drop & Charging Station Attacks
threats.summary: Found USB drives or 'free charging' cables install malware (BadUSB) or skim data from phones. Parking lot and conference drops still work against curious users.
how_it_works: Labeled drive: 'Confidential Salaries' left in lobby.
USB wall charger with hidden data pins (juice jacking).
Rubber ducky keystroke injection on unlock.
Malware autoruns on older systems; social engineering on modern.
real_world: Red team exercises regularly succeed with drops.
Public USB ports in transit hubs flagged by CISA guidance.
Corporate espionage variant targets trade secrets.
red_flags: Unknown USB device free for taking.
Public charging without USB data blocker.
Prompt to install driver from inserted drive.
what_to_do: Never plug unknown USB; turn in to IT.
Charge with own AC adapter or USB condom/data blocker.
Disable autorun; full scan if mistake made.
threats.tell_others: Don't plug in random USB sticks you find — they're often traps. Charge your phone from the wall, not unknown USB ports.

threats.title: Stalkerware / Partner Spyware on Phones
threats.summary: Hidden apps track location, messages, and calls — installed by abusive partners or parents without consent. Not 'security' — illegal in many jurisdictions when non-consensual.
how_it_works: Brief physical access → install mSpy-like app or MDM profile.
iCloud credential theft enables backup monitoring.
Fake 'antivirus' or 'find my friend' cover story.
Data exfil to attacker dashboard.
real_world: Coalition Against Stalkerware; NNEDV tech safety resources.
Domestic violence survivors primary affected population.
Employers illegally monitoring workers in some cases.
red_flags: Battery drain, hot phone, unknown MDM/config profile.
Partner knows conversations they weren't present for.
2FA prompts you didn't initiate.
what_to_do: Use safe device at DV shelter/resource — don't tip off abuser.
Factory reset from trusted network; new Apple/Google account.
Legal aid and police where safe.
threats.tell_others: If someone had your phone alone, they may have installed tracking. Domestic violence hotlines help plan safe device checks.

threats.title: Elder Financial Abuse (All Channels)
threats.summary: Scammers and sometimes trusted caregivers exploit cognitive decline, isolation, or tech unfamiliarity — via phone, in-person, or legal document manipulation.
how_it_works: Repeated small withdrawals escalate to deed transfer.
Isolation: 'don't tell family, they'll put you in home'.
Tech support + romance + government scams compound.
Powers of attorney obtained under undue influence.
real_world: Adult protective services caseloads rising with aging population.
Bank 'trusted contact' and elder hold policies expanding.
Family members sometimes perpetrators — not only strangers.
red_flags: New 'best friend' or partner isolated from family.
Unusual wire/gift card purchases.
Mail redirected; statements stop arriving.
what_to_do: Family: regular low-judgment check-ins on finances.
Banks: report suspected exploitation.
Legal: capacity assessment before major asset changes.
threats.tell_others: Check on older relatives' finances like health — scammers call daily. A five-minute conversation can stop a six-figure loss.

threats.title: AI Voice Clone & Deepfake Vishing (2024–2025)
threats.summary: Short social clips train AI to clone a boss or family member's voice. Calls or voicemails demand urgent wire transfers or gift cards.
how_it_works: Voice sample from TikTok/YouTube/LinkedIn video.
Real-time cloned call: 'I'm in a meeting — wire this now.'
Video call deepfake variants in high-value BEC.
real_world: Public cases of six-figure transfers authorized after cloned CEO voice.
Family emergency scams using cloned child voice.
red_flags: Urgent money request breaking normal procedure.
Refusal to use established approval channel.
Call quality odd but voice familiar.
what_to_do: Callback using known number — not one provided on call.
Establish verbal code word for family financial emergencies.
Corporate: wire policy requires second channel approval.
threats.tell_others: A voice that sounds exactly like your boss or kid can be faked now. Always call back on a number you already trust before sending money.

threats.title: Grandparent / Family Emergency Scam
threats.summary: Caller claims to be grandchild in jail, car accident, or kidnapping — needs cash, gift cards, or wire immediately. AI voice clones now make the 'grandchild' speak directly.
how_it_works: Cold call: 'Grandma, it's me — don't tell mom.'
Handoff to fake lawyer/police demanding secrecy.
Courier pickup of cash or crypto ATM instructions.
AI variant: cloned voice on the line.
real_world: Elder fraud hotlines report this among most common calls.
Losses spike around holidays and school terms.
Police departments publicly state they never demand gift cards.
red_flags: Secrecy demanded from family.
Payment via gift cards, crypto ATM, or courier cash.
Caller blocks callback to child's real phone.
what_to_do: Hang up; call grandchild directly.
Ask question only real relative would answer.
Police non-emergency line to verify — not number caller gives.
threats.tell_others: Scammers pretend to be your grandkid in trouble. Hang up and call your family directly — real police don't take payment in gift cards.

threats.title: Vishing — Fake Bank & Government Calls
threats.summary: Caller ID spoofing makes your bank or IRS appear to call. They invent fraud on your account and walk you through 'securing' funds — into their account.
how_it_works: Spoofed caller ID matches bank's published number.
Create panic: unauthorized wire, warrant, frozen SSN.
Instruct victim to Zelle/wire/crypto 'to safe account'.
real_world: FBI IC3: billions lost to vishing + pig butchering combos.
Elder-targeted 'your grandson is in jail' variants.
red_flags: Call asks for OTP, PIN, or to move money to 'safe' account.
Pressure to stay on line while you go to bank.
what_to_do: Hang up; call number on back of debit card.
Never wire on instructions from inbound call.
Banks don't ask for full passwords or 2FA by phone.
threats.tell_others: Your bank will never ask you to wire money to yourself for safety. Hang up and call the number on your card.
